referents.why: first common singular 'me' inside Pharaoh's speech (cl1 introduces it); the speaker is Pharaoh, not the builder's 'he' of the saying clause
first common singular suffix 'my' on 'people' inside Pharaoh's speech; refers to the speaker
third masculine singular wayyiqtol 'he said'; the subject named in cl0 (Pharaoh) continues, since cl0 and cl1 share the subject
referents.category: implied subject of a speech-introducing verb

referents.why: second masculine plural imperative; the 'you' is those Pharaoh summoned and addressed, Moses and Aaron together
referents.category: implied subject of a command to the addressees

referents.why: third masculine singular jussive 'let him remove the frogs'; what is asked in prayer 'to Yahweh' is done by Yahweh, the only sensible doer among the singular masculine candidates
referents.category: implied subject of a jussive after a prayer command

referents.why: first common singular cohortative 'I will let go' inside Pharaoh's speech; the speaker, not the builder's 'he' of cl1
third masculine plural jussive 'that they may sacrifice'; 'the people' (your people, the object of cl4) is a collective noun taking a plural verb, and are the ones sent out to sacrifice
referents.category: plural verb with collective noun as referent

links.why: reverse duplicate of the cl0 to cl1 link; the summoning comes first and the saying follows, so the link runs from cl0 only
links.category: duplicate link in the wrong direction

links.why: two wayyiqtol clauses in sequence: he summoned, and then he said
a waw joining an imperative to a jussive in a different person (you to he) is 'so that', not a plain and; replaced by purpose
links.category: plain and read for change of person after a command

links.why: waw plus first-person cohortative, a promise after the jussive; the form marks no condition, so the plain 'and' is kept rather than 'if'
links.category: promise after a request joined by plain and

links.why: waw plus a jussive in a different person (I to they) states what the release is for; replaced by purpose
links.category: plain and read for change of person

links.why: command to pray, then waw + jussive in a different person: 'pray ... that he may remove the frogs'
links.category: command then jussive in a different person

links.why: 'I will let your people go, that they may sacrifice': waw + jussive in a different person says what the release is for; the first term is a cohortative, not a command (see none_fit)
the saying clause and what was said, which opens with a command (the pray command and its aim) inside the speech

groups.why: Pharaoh (sender) speaks to Moses and Aaron (addressees, whom cl0 says he summoned); the parts are the command group and the promise with its purpose; cl2 and cl3 sit inside the imperative group, so they are no longer direct parts
groups.category: turn with its addressee stated by the previous clause

groups.why: one command (pray) and the jussive that states its aim (that he may remove the frogs); cl3 is an aim of the command, not a second part
groups.category: command with its aim as a jussive in another person

groups.why: cl3 is a third-person jussive, not a command given to the addressees, and cl4 is a first-person promise; neither makes an imperative group
cl4 is the speaker's own cohortative promise, not a command, so there is no imperative group; its relation to cl5 is a purpose link

none_fit.what: The release in cl4 is promised in exchange for the removal in cl3 ('pray, and then I will let them go'); the form carries no condition (plain waw, cohortative), and no link type covers a promise or offer made on the strength of a request being met, so the plain 'and' is kept.

The purpose type names a command as its first term, but here the first term is a cohortative promise (I will let go) and the clause after it a jussive (that they may sacrifice); the sense of purpose is plain and the closest type is used, but the wording of the type does not cover this case.
